title: KV prefetch rabbit hole — scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Spike to understand whether proactive KV prefetching (on request start) can reduce p99 on medium-length chat traces without blowing up GPU memory or throughput.
- Observed two customer clusters: short-turn chat (<=128 tokens) and long-turn assistant sessions (~2k tokens). Prefetch benefit likely only for the latter or for warmed-up sequences.
- Hypothesis: Prefetching the next N KV blocks when first request arrives reduces serialization stalls on the first few generation steps for continued sessions. Trade-offs: extra memory + bandwidth + potential wasted prefetch on single-turn requests.

Quick notes from last run (2025-02-18, 02:15 UTC):
- Test harness: local-mini (4xA100-40G), runtime branch: prefetch/opt-187
- Workload: mixed-chat-1k.json (50% short, 30% medium, 20% long; 500 sessions)
- Config: prefetch_enabled=true, prefetch_blocks=3, prefetch_async=true
- Result summary: median latency unchanged; p95 improved ~6%; p99 improved ~11% for long sessions only; throughput drop ~2.3% under 1% tail-saturation.
- Memory: per-GPU extra ~370MB when prefetch_blocks=3 (KV stored in host pinned buffers), still within headroom.
- Unexpected: a small subset (~4%) of short sessions had increased latency due to host->device transfer contention during bursts.

Repro steps (local):
1) checkout runtime branch: git fetch && git checkout prefetch/opt-187
2) start local harness: ./tools/run_local_harness --config tests/mixed-chat-1k.json --nodes 1
3) enable tracing for sample 003: export RL_TRACE=sample-003 && tail -f /tmp/runtime-trace.log
4) inspect nvtop and nvidia-smi during run; note host pinned mem rising.

Hypotheses / ideas to validate:
- H1: Async prefetch with a low-concurrency host DMA queue reduces the contention seen by short sessions (schedule at lower priority).
- H2: Prefetch heuristics should be based on session length estimate (from request metadata or early token pattern) instead of global flag.
- H3: For models with big KV stripe size (like >512 dim), prefetch_blocks=1 gives ~80% of p99 benefit with much less memory.
- H4: Use per-connection budget; if connection idle > X ms then cancel in-flight prefetch to reclaim memory.

Mini-experiments to run (priority):
- EXP-A: prefetch_blocks=1, async=true, host-queue-depth=2 (run same harness). Target: p99 improvement with <150MB memory.
- EXP-B: conditional prefetch only when session_metadata.estimated_length > 256 tokens. Evaluate false positives/negatives.
- EXP-C: throttle prefetch bandwidth to 50% during high short-session bursts (simulate spike). See if short-session penalty disappears.
- EXP-D: measure host->device PCIe stalls with perf counters when prefetch enabled (capture with nvprof / Nsight counters).

Open risks / questions:
- Q1: Does prefetch interact poorly with KV eviction? If prefetch pushes out hot entries for other sessions, we could create regressions. Need to capture eviction logs.
- Q2: For dedicated pools with smaller instance sizes, does extra host memory become a blocker for multi-tenant packing?
- Q3: Security: do we prefetch only same-tenant sequences? Yes, but verify there is no cross-tenant cache leakage path.

Quick todo (rough timeline):
- [ ] Run EXP-A (low) — 2025-02-19 (Mina)
- [ ] Add session-length heuristic toggle feature flag (runtime flag + simple estimator) — 2025-02-20 (Rajiv)
- [ ] Add prefetch cancellation on idle (prototype) — 2025-02-21 (Evelyn)
- [ ] Collect eviction traces + overlay with prefetch timeline (SRE assist) — 2025-02-22
- [ ] Draft short doc for product tradeoffs (1-pager) — 2025-02-24

Notes to self (kernel-level observations):
- When prefetch async is true we see more host pinned buffers in 'smaps' (host pinned allocations remain longer). Might need LRU trimming.
- Kernel-level DMA thread spikes coincide with high arrival bursts; causes slight jitter in kernel scheduling. Consider lower-priority niceness for DMA thread.
- NUMA: pin host pinned buffers to the same NUMA node as GPU to reduce latency; current allocator is round-robin which likely adds 20–30us per fetch.

Commands I used (copyable):
- ./tools/run_local_harness --config tests/mixed-chat-1k.json --nodes 1 --env PREFETCH_BLOCKS=3
- sudo perf record -a -g -- ./tools/run_local_harness --config tests/mixed-chat-1k.json
- python scripts/trace_overlay.py --traces /tmp/runtime-trace-* --out /tmp/overlay.html

Metrics to capture next runs (automatic):
- p50/p95/p99 by session length bucket (<=128, 129–512, >512)
- per-GPU host-pinned-memory over time
- number of cancelled prefetches
- eviction rate (entries/sec) + collateral misses

Short brainstorm (future ideas):
- Aggressive micro-prefetch: instead of blocks, prefetch only first M-keywords likely to be needed (requires model token-coverage heuristics).
- Hybrid caching: maintain a small per-AI-tenant warm-KV of last-called keys for faster resume.
- Cost-aware router: route suspected long sessions to nodes with prefetch capacity enabled.

Scratch log (timestamps):
- 2025-02-18 01:58 — started local run, saw p99 drop on long sessions
- 2025-02-18 02:05 — spotted short-session regressions; started perf
- 2025-02-18 02:35 — Rajiv suggested session-length heuristic; penciled EXP-B
- 2025-02-18 03:10 — wrote initial PR and pushed small allocator tweak

Unresolved TODOs (for next async pairing):

- add telemetry labels so we can split prefetch traffic in datadog/dashboard
- checklist for rollout: canary in dedicated pool -> metrics gating -> staged enable in hosted

End of scratchpad.
